title: A restart inside an epoch loses a live call's media secret; decide what the call does about it
design:
Found 2026-11-24 closing bead mimid-1wgh.4.82 (the §4.4 safe exporter),
and now pinned by a test:
crates/mimid-agent-core/tests/call_rooms.rs
an_agent_that_restarts_inside_an_epoch_loses_the_media_secret.

WHAT HAPPENS. Agent::media_secret reads SafeExportSecret(media_keys) once
per epoch and keeps the result in memory (Agent::media_secrets), because
mls-extensions-11 §4.4's exporter punctures the Exporter Tree leaf when it
is read and a second read in the same epoch fails. The puncture is written
to the store; the secret never is (decision: it is a secret, and
docs/design/... keeps media key material out of the database). So after a
restart:

  media_secret(call) -> AgentError::Mls

and it keeps failing until the call room's epoch moves. A member who was
in the call before the restart is then no better off than one who never
joined.

THIS IS §4.4 WORKING, NOT A DEFECT. If a restart could re-derive the
secret, the source key material would not have been deleted, which is
precisely what §4.4 exists to prevent ("the MLS implementation MUST regard
that component's exported secret as 'consumed', and delete any source key
material"). The behaviour is correct. The question is what a CALL does
about it, which no draft answers.

THE READINGS, none of them obviously right:

(a) COMMIT TO ROLL THE EPOCH. On a restart with a live call, the agent
    sends an empty Commit in the call room; the new epoch has an unread
    leaf, every member re-derives, and the media key rolls. Costs a round
    trip and a hub interaction per restart, and only a member who can
    commit can do it. Two members restarting at once race, which MLS
    resolves (first valid Commit per epoch wins) but which means the loser
    waits another round trip. Probably the right answer, and it needs no
    new wire format and no stored secret.

(b) PERSIST THE SECRET, encrypted at rest alongside the MLS state. Cheap
    and immediate, and it gives up exactly the forward security §4.4 was
    chosen for: an attacker with the database gets every live call's media
    key. Against AGENTS.md's handling of key material. Mentioned only to
    be rejected.

(c) DO NOTHING, and let the media layer notice. A call whose key cannot be
    derived is a call that fails; the client re-invites or restarts the
    call, which creates a new room with a new group. Honest, and today's
    behaviour. The cost is that a crash during a call is unrecoverable
    from the user's point of view, for no reason they can see.

(d) READ IT LAZILY, so the secret is exported only when a media stack
    actually asks. Does not help after the first ask, which is the case
    this bead is about, but it does shrink the window: an agent that
    restarts before anyone joined the media has not punctured anything.
    Worth doing whichever of the above wins.

MY RECOMMENDATION: (a), with (d) as a free improvement, and (c) as the
fallback when this agent cannot commit in the call room. Not implemented:
(a) changes what a restart does on the wire, which is a decision rather
than a fix, and the agent currently has no notion of "a live call" to
trigger it from -- that arrives with bead mimid-1wgh.114.1's announcement.

BLOCKED ON, in practice: mimid-1wgh.114.1 (the announcement, which is what
tells an agent a call is live) and therefore on mimid-1wgh.128.
notes:
DECIDED by Mark, 2026-11-24: reading (a) with (d), and (c) as the
fallback. Reading (b), persisting the secret, is rejected and should not
be revisited: it gives away exactly the forward security §4.4 was chosen
for, and a copy of the database would hold every live call's media key.

WHAT TO BUILD, when bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 gives the agent a notion of a
live call to trigger from:

1. ROLL THE EPOCH ON RESTART. When the agent starts and finds a live call
   in a room it holds, it sends an empty Commit in the CALL room (not the
   parent). The new epoch has an unread Exporter Tree leaf, every member
   re-derives, and the media key rolls. Nothing new on the wire: an empty
   Commit is an ordinary Commit, and a rolling media key on a membership
   change is already the designed behaviour (mimid-agent-core/src/media.rs).

2. READ THE SECRET LAZILY. Agent::media_secret is called when something
   actually needs the key, not when the call room is created, so an agent
   that restarts before anyone started media has punctured nothing and
   needs no Commit at all. Worth doing on its own: it shrinks the window
   this bead is about rather than only recovering from it. Check what
   VtcBackend::export_media_secret and the VTCCall projection do today,
   since a projection that exports eagerly would defeat it.

3. FALL BACK TO FAILING, reading (c), when this agent cannot commit in the
   call room: the room policy may not let it, or the Commit may lose the
   race. The error must reach the client as "this call cannot continue"
   rather than a silence, so the user starts a new call knowing why. A new
   call is a new room with a new group, so it does work.

RACES ARE FINE AND NEED NO SPECIAL HANDLING. Two members restarting at
once both commit; MLS picks the first valid Commit per epoch in hub order
(AGENTS.md's security invariant), the loser processes the winner's Commit
and re-derives from the epoch it lands in. The loser waits one more round
trip, which is the cost of the simplest correct thing.

WHAT TO WATCH FOR WHEN BUILDING IT:

  - A restart loop must not become a Commit loop. If the Commit fails, do
    not retry on a timer: fall back to (3). The outbox already resends
    the same bytes after a crash (docs/design/agent-frontends.md §3 step
    10), so a Commit that was sent before the crash must not be sent
    again as a new one.
  - The agent must not roll the epoch of a room merely because it holds a
    media secret for it. Only a LIVE call justifies the traffic; every
    other room's secret can stay unread.
  - A test belongs beside
    tests/call_rooms.rs an_agent_that_restarts_inside_an_epoch_loses_the_media_secret,
    which pins today's behaviour. That test asserts the failure, so
    implementing this changes it: the honest shape is to keep it for the
    case where the agent cannot commit, and add one where it can and the
    call continues.
CORRECTION to my own implementation note above, 2026-11-25, before any code. THE TRIGGER I WROTE WOULD BREAK DECISION mimid-1wgh.117.

I wrote: "When the agent starts and finds a live call in a room it holds, it sends an empty Commit in the CALL room." That requires the agent to decide a call is LIVE. The only thing it could decide that from after a restart is the chat: a start announcement with no matching ended one. Decision mimid-1wgh.117 forbids exactly that inference -- "its ABSENCE MEANS 'not known', never 'still going'" -- and a client that showed a live badge on that basis is the mistake .117 exists to prevent. An agent that sent a Commit on it would be making the same mistake with traffic instead of pixels.

Mark's decision is unaffected: roll the epoch. What changes is WHEN.

THE TRIGGER IS A FAILED EXPORT, not a startup scan. Agent::media_secret already answers from a per-epoch cache and exports when it misses. When that export fails BECAUSE THE LEAF IS CONSUMED, something is asking for a key for an epoch whose secret this agent no longer holds -- which is the restart case and nothing else. The ask itself is the evidence, so nothing is inferred about liveness, and the agent never sends a Commit for a call nobody wants.

This also merges readings (a) and (d) into one mechanism instead of two: the secret is exported when something asks (which is already true), and the roll happens on the one failure that a roll fixes. Nothing scans at startup, so there is no "notion of a live call" to build, and this bead no longer waits on anything.

THE FAILURE IS DISTINGUISHABLE, checked rather than assumed: openmls returns SafeExportSecretError::ApplicationExportTree(ApplicationExportTreeError::PuncturedInput) for a consumed leaf, and openmls's own test asserts it (openmls/src/group/mls_group/tests_and_kats/tests/mls_group.rs:476). The other variants -- GroupState for a removed member, Unsupported for a group with no Exporter Tree, Storage -- must NOT roll: none is fixed by a new epoch.

WHAT THIS MAKES TRUE, and it is worth stating because it is a surprise: reading the media secret can send a Commit to the room. A read with a write as its side effect. It is bounded -- after a roll the secret is cached for that epoch, so a second ask is answered from memory and sends nothing -- but it means VTCCall/exportMediaSecret can cost a round trip and move the room's epoch. Agent::media_secret becomes async for it; Store::media_secret already is.

A roll that fails falls back to reading (c): the error reaches the client as "this call cannot continue", and no retry on a timer, so a restart loop cannot become a Commit loop.
THE SHAPE, settled 2026-11-25 after Mark asked what the Right Thing was, and it is better than either of my two previous notes. The deciding fact was in the code, not in reasoning: VtcBackend::export_media_secret already takes the epoch the client believes the call is in and answers either the secret or EpochMoved(current) -- 'tell it which one is current rather than hand it a secret nobody else is using'.

THE REAL DEFECT is that the restart case is UNREPRESENTABLE in that contract. The client asks for epoch N; the current epoch IS still N; the agent simply cannot serve N. There is no truthful EpochMoved to send, so today it becomes a Forbidden with an error string.

ROLLING THE EPOCH MAKES IT REPRESENTABLE. After the roll the current epoch is N+1, the client asked about N, and EpochMoved(N+1) is literally true. So:

  - Agent::media_secret and Store::media_secret STAY PURE READS and keep failing. No read with a hidden write, which was the wart I was about to ask Mark to accept.
  - VtcBackend::export_media_secret, which already owns the epoch conversation, rolls on that ONE failure and answers EpochMoved(N+1).
  - The client re-asks for N+1 and gets the secret by the ordinary path, through code it already has, because EpochMoved is already in the surface.

No new error type, no draft addition, no new client obligation.

NOTHING IS INFERRED ABOUT LIVENESS, which is what decision mimid-1wgh.117 requires and what my chat-scanning version broke: the client's ask supplies 'someone wants this' and the puncture in our own store supplies 'and I lost it'. Both are local and certain.

IT SELF-BOUNDS. A second ask for N finds the epoch already N+1, so the existing 'wanted != current' check fires BEFORE any export and no second roll happens. One roll per loss, at most.

THREE CONDITIONS:
  1. Roll only on SafeExportSecretError::ApplicationExportTree(ApplicationExportTreeError::PuncturedInput). Never on GroupState (removed), Unsupported (no Exporter Tree) or Storage: a new epoch fixes none of them.
  2. No retry on a timer, so a restart loop cannot become a Commit loop.
  3. A roll that fails returns the error to the client as 'this call cannot continue', reading (c), rather than a silence.
